title: HTTP and REST APIs in one screen
rememberThis: HTTP = request (method, URL, headers, body) + response (status, headers, body) mapped to HttpContext.
REST uses noun URLs and stateless handlers — verbs live in HTTP methods, not /cancelOrder paths.
Return honest status codes: 4xx client fault, 5xx server fault — never 200 with { error: true }.
Version breaking changes (URL or header); measure old version traffic before removal.
POST payments need Idempotency-Key + stored replay; ETags and Cache-Control save bandwidth and origin load.
bullets: GET is safe and cacheable; POST creates and is not idempotent without an idempotency key.
401 = missing/invalid auth; 403 = authenticated but forbidden; 409 = conflict; 422 = business validation.
URL versioning (/api/v2/) is CDN-friendly; header versioning keeps URLs clean but is easier to omit.
OpenAPI documents contracts — annotate ProducesResponseType for errors; diff spec in CI.
Idempotency store: key + request hash + response + TTL in Redis; 409 when key reused with different body.
Express parallels: req/res headers, router mounting, res.status(), swagger-ui-express, apicache.
